chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Salih, the mawla of Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who died and left wealth, and left behind his sister and his mawali (clients/freedmen). He said, 'The wealth belongs to his sister.'

key_terms.مَوَالِيَهُ: his mawali (clients or freedmen under his patronage)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate if a man dies leaving only his sister and his mawali?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the hierarchy of inheritance between a sister and the *mawali* (clients) of the deceased, ruling that the sister takes the entire estate. This establishes the principle that the sister, as a closer kin (*dhawu al-arham*), supersedes the *mawali* in this specific configuration, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the rights of maternal or paternal sisters versus freedmen's patrons. The ruling highlights the nuanced application of Quranic inheritance verses where specific heirs exclude others based on proximity and gender.
